name: mlton
desc: Whole-program, optimizing compiler for Standard ML
why: Whole-program optimising compiler for Standard ML, an old-school functional language with a distinctive compilation approach.

brief.what_it_is: MLton is a whole-program optimizing compiler for Standard ML. You give it SML source (and ML Basis files for libraries), and it produces standalone native executables that the homepage describes as small and fast. It also ships a Standard ML environment with the Basis Library and tools: the mllex lexer generator, the mlyacc parser generator, the mlprof source-level profiler, and the mlnlffigen foreign-function-interface generator.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames MLton as a compiler that generates small executables with excellent runtime performance, and as a feature-rich Standard ML programming environment with full SML97 support.
brief.how_it_works: Because it is whole-program, MLton compiles the entire program together so it can optimize across module boundaries. The README credits untagged and unboxed native integers, reals and words, unboxed native arrays, GMP-based arbitrary-precision arithmetic, and several selectable code generation and garbage collection strategies. The README does not go into more detail on the optimization pipeline.

commands_seen.context: Builds MLton from source with no configuration on typical platforms; artifacts land under ./build, and the new compiler is at ./build/bin/mlton.

commands_seen.cmd: $ make CC=clang WITH_GMP_DIR=/opt/gmp MLTON_COMPILE_ARGS="-codegen c" all
commands_seen.context: Example build that picks clang, points at a GMP install in /opt/gmp, and passes -codegen c to the compiler used to build the new mlton.
Builds the documentation; optional, and needs TeX, AsciiDoctor, Rouge and an image tool.
Installs MLton to /usr/local after make all, or after make update for a binary package.
Installs MLton under a custom prefix instead of /usr/local.
For the binary package route: configures the extracted package to use clang and a custom GMP location.

brief.install_notes: Building from source needs GCC or Clang with -std=gnu11 support, GMP, GNU Make, GNU Bash, binutils (ar, ranlib, strip), and common Unix utilities. Bootstrapping needs a Standard ML compiler: MLton itself is recommended, while SML/NJ, Poly/ML and MLKit are supported but not recommended. Hardware: at least 1GB RAM on 32-bit or 2GB on 64-bit. Pre-built binaries come from OS package managers or from mlton.org for some platforms. A binary .tgz or .tbz package can be extracted anywhere and run in place (./bin/mlton), after make update. Default install goes to /usr/local, and PREFIX changes that.
brief.standout: Whole-program compilation to small native executables, with a full SML Basis Library, a C FFI, and bundled lexer, parser and profiler tools, is unusual for an SML implementation. The README also has no Standard ML-specific warnings; it just lists what the compiler produces.
brief.status: maintained. The homepage says 'Last updated Mon Dec 30 07:22:35 2024' and points at the MLton 20241230 release. The GitHub repo shows 10,311 commits, 1.1k stars, 139 forks and a master branch with active directories. I did not see an exact date of the most recent commit.
brief.caveats: Bootstrapping and building need GMP and a C compiler that supports gnu11. The README says the non-MLton bootstrap compilers are supported but not recommended. Optional docs need a heavy TeX and AsciiDoctor toolchain. The README gives no platform list beyond saying it 'runs on a wide variety of platforms'. I did not check the license file, which is in the repo root.
